EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows (i) a very strong band at 2247 cm⁻¹ that lies at the high-frequency edge of the Si–H stretching region (GFQ-004, 2100–2200 cm⁻¹; organosilanes with electron-withdrawing alkyl substituents can appear slightly above 2220 cm⁻¹), (ii) a distinct band at 918 cm⁻¹ that coincides with the characteristic Si–H bending/rocking region (GFQ-004, 890–930 cm⁻¹), and (iii) a medium band at 548 cm⁻¹ consistent with Si–C stretching vibrations in alkyl-silanes. These three mutually reinforcing silicon-hydride signatures point to the only candidates that contain an Si–H bond (1 and 3). The remaining intense C–H stretching bands at 2997, 2933 and 2887 cm⁻¹ match the aliphatic C–H stretches expected for a small alkylsilane (GFQ-003). The spectrum contains no ≡C–H stretch (~3300 cm⁻¹) or other features diagnostic of nitriles or alcohol O–H groups, disfavouring candidates 4–10. Between the two Si–H candidates, 1 ([2H]CC[SiH](C)C) has fewer heavy-atom vibrations and would be expected to give a simpler Raman pattern, consistent with the limited number of observed mid- and low-frequency peaks (only 13 total). Therefore candidate 1 is the best match.
